title: Network Threats and Defensive Strategies
summary: A comprehensive overview of network threats detailing primary attack objectives, main attack pillars, specific threat categories, and key defensive strategies and countermeasures.

sections.title: Understanding Network Threats
paragraphs: A network threat is any malicious attempt to compromise, disrupt, or gain unauthorized access to network infrastructure, transmitted data, or connected devices.

sections.title: The Three Main Attack Pillars
list: Software & Code (Malware): Exploiting system software, OS flaws, and unpatched applications.
Network & Traffic Infrastructure: Intercepting network packets, flooding bandwidth, or hijacking DNS.
Human & Identity Factors: Manipulating human behavior and stealing credentials to bypass perimeter defenses.

sections.title: Malware Attacks
list: Ransomware: Encrypts network shares & critical files, demanding extortion payments for keys.
Spyware & Trojans: Disguised software that secretly logs keypresses and harvests credentials.
Network Worms: Self-replicating malware spreading laterally across connected nodes without user action.

sections.title: Infrastructure & Traffic
list: DDoS Attacks: Floods network bandwidth or server sockets with botnet traffic to cause severe outages.
Man-in-the-Middle (MitM): Intercepts and alters active session packets over unencrypted or rogue networks.
DNS Spoofing: Corrupts domain resolution caches to silently redirect traffic to malicious sites.

sections.title: Social & Identity
list: Phishing: Deceptive emails designed to trick users into revealing access secrets.
Credential Stuffing: Automated injection of leaked credentials across corporate login portals.
Insider Threats: Malicious or careless actions by internal staff with valid system permissions.

sections.title: Defensive Strategies & Countermeasures
paragraphs: Best practices and architectural principles to mitigate network threats.

sections.title: Zero Trust Architecture
paragraphs: Never trust, always verify. Enforce strict identity validation and access controls for every device and user attempt, inside or outside the network perimeter.

sections.title: Multi-Factor Authentication (MFA)
paragraphs: Requires multiple verification factors (MFA/2FA) across all endpoints and administrative access portals to neutralize stolen credentials.

sections.title: Network Segmentation
paragraphs: Divides networks into isolated sub-zones to contain breaches, preventing lateral movement of malware or attackers across internal subnets.

sections.title: Continuous Monitoring & Patching
paragraphs: Deploys Intrusion Detection/Prevention Systems (IDS/IPS), SIEM monitoring, and automated patch management to resolve vulnerabilities rapidly.
